items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: Now, another one that was his student, I was a very small boy at the time, it was Albert France.

ctx.x: Of course, money was a little more valuable then than now, but still it was a low price for a famous teacher.

And the last student of his that really turned out to be a real nice drummer was Freddie Coleman. That's the last one. Coleman was his last student that I can remember. Now, another one that was his student, I was a very small boy at the time, it was Albert France. I don't know if you knew Albert France. Yeah, we interviewed him a couple of weeks ago. Albert was one of his students. Ernest Trepanyu was another one of his students. And so many of the boys were students. In fact, most of the drums in that period…

And if they didn't, I'm going to say quite a few of them, maybe like Baby Dodds even, who went to Chicago. I think he only had a few lessons. He wouldn't tell us too much about it. I think your father didn't get along too well with him. He didn't learn to read fast enough or something. Well, it could have been that. He was kind of impatient. I'll tell you that. That was one thing why I didn't want to learn how to play a drum. Because he was a little impatient. Even if they only took a few lessons, there's maybe…
